q: 51. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day, pessimistic time is 11 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Expected time formula is t_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p) / 6. Substituting the values: t_e = (1 + 4(3) + 11) / 6 = 24 / 6 = 4 days.

q: 52. Of the following, the PERT event is
explain: An event represents a moment in time (a state of accomplishment), whereas activities represent operations that consume time. 'Concrete cured' indicates a completed state/milestone.

q: 53. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT accounts for uncertainty by combining three time estimates: Optimistic (t_o), Pessimistic (t_p), and Most Likely (t_m).

q: 54. In PERT analysis, the start and end of event is represented by
explain: Events (nodes) in PERT mark the instantaneous starting or ending points of activities in the network diagram.

q: 55. The probability of completion of any activity within its expected time in PERT is
explain: In PERT, expected time (t_e) corresponds to the 50th percentile of the Beta probability distribution curve.

q: 56. If the probability factor is zero, the chances of completing the project in scheduled time are
explain: A probability factor (Z-score) of 0 means the scheduled time equals the expected time, which gives a 50% chance of completion on a normal curve.

q: 57. You are going to design a new computer programme, which would you like to prefer?
explain: Software development and R&D activities involve significant time uncertainties, making PERT the ideal technique.

q: 58. Bar chart is used for minor project, CPM is used for repetitive work while PERT is used for
options: limited time and unlimited resources types of work
uncertainty time and resources types of work
explain: PERT was created specifically to handle probabilistic and uncertain project durations and resource demands.

q: 59. Standard deviation when the optimistic time is 1 day, pessimistic time is 11 days and most likely time is 3 days
explain: Standard deviation formula in PERT is σ = (t_p - t_o) / 6. Substituting values: σ = (11 - 1) / 6 = 10 / 6 ≈ 1.67 days.

q: 60. In PERT analysis the actual performance of task is known as
explain: In PERT terminology, milestones marking the completion or actual performance point of tasks are identified as events.

q: 61. Line of balance technique is used for
options: comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: Line of Balance (LOB) is a visual management tool used mainly in repetitive construction to compare actual site progress against planned schedules.

q: 62. In PERT, optimistic time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Optimistic time (t_o) is defined as the minimum possible duration required to complete an activity if everything goes exceptionally well.

q: 63. In PERT, pessimistic time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Pessimistic time (t_p) is the maximum possible duration required to complete an activity under adverse conditions.

q: 64. In PERT, the most likely time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Most likely time (t_m) represents the modal duration—the time needed under normal, average operational conditions.

q: 65. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is equal to
explain: The formula for expected (average) time in a Beta distribution is t_e = (a + 4m + b) / 6.

q: 66. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow a
explain: Individual activity durations in PERT are modeled using a unimodal Beta distribution curve.

q: 67. Negative slack occurs
options: when latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack indicates a project delay or shortage of resources where the allowable time (TL) is less than the expected time (TE).

q: 68. A stage or point where all previous jobs merging in it are completed and all further jobs bursting out are still to be completed is known as a
explain: An event acts as a juncture node where predecessor activities converge (merge) and successor activities originate (burst).

q: 69. The latest allowable time for any event i is equal to
explain: During backward pass calculations, the Latest Allowable Occurring Time T_L for an event is computed as the minimum of (T_L^j - t^ij).

q: 70. SLACK time refers to an
explain: Slack is associated with events (nodes), whereas Float is associated with activities.

q: 71. The minimum number of years required to complete any research project may be
explain: Research duration depends on the specific scope, complexity, and available funding, meaning it can vary widely.

q: 72. An event is indicated on the network by a number enclosed in
explain: Network conventions typically use circles, but squares, triangles, or ellipses can also represent nodes.

q: 73. Slack time in PERT analysis
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: Critical path events are defined by having the minimum (often zero or most negative) slack in the network.

q: 74. The area under the beta-curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time (t_e) represents the mean duration, bisecting the probability density area under the curve into 50% regions.

q: 75. For a beta-distribution curve, if t_o is the optimistic time and t_p the pessimistic time then the standard deviation will be equal to
explain: Standard deviation in PERT is defined as one-sixth of the total spread between pessimistic and optimistic time estimates: σ = (t_p - t_o) / 6.

q: 76. For a curve, larger the variance
explain: Variance measures data dispersion; higher variance signifies wider time uncertainty in completing the task.

q: 77. If an activity has its optimistic, most likely and pessimistic time are 2, 4 & 6 respectively, then its expected time and variance are respectively
explain: Expected time t_e = (2 + 4(4) + 6)/6 = 24/6 = 4. Standard deviation σ = (6 - 2)/6 = 4/6 = 2/3. Variance σ² = (2/3)² = 4/9.

q: 78. CPM means
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method.

q: 79. A CPM family includes
explain: The CPM family encompasses analysis, plotting, and resource scheduling variants.

q: 80. In CPM analysis
explain: CPM is an activity-oriented, deterministic system (fixed durations) that uses arrows to represent activities in Activity-on-Arrow diagrams.

q: 81. Choose the incorrect statement
options: arrow representing activity in CPM network is drawn without any scale
head of an activity represents the finish of an activity
tail of an activity represents the start of an activity
explain: Statements (a), (b), and (c) are all correct CPM network conventions, making (d) the correct choice.

q: 82. The occurrence of the starting of an activity is called its
explain: The node at the origin of an activity arrow is its tail event, signifying its commencement.

q: 83. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The arrowhead node indicates the head event, signifying completion of the activity.

q: 84. The difference between total float and free float is called interfering float which is nothing but the
explain: Interfering Float = Total Float - Free Float = Head Event Slack.

q: 85. CPM adopts
explain: CPM assumes known activity durations, following a deterministic model.

q: 86. CPM network is
explain: CPM focuses on project activities and their required time/costs, making it activity-oriented.

q: 87. The scheduled completion time of an operation in CPM chart is mentioned on
options: left top corner outside the circle
left top corner inside the circle
explain: In node diagram conventions, timing indicators (like Earliest Time) are noted on the upper left side outside the event node.

q: 88. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circle
explain: In left-to-right network flow diagramming, the task on the left precedes and must be completed before downstream tasks.

q: 89. Number of pre-operation associated with an operation may be
explain: An activity can depend on multiple preceding activities in complex dependency networks.

q: 90. In a network, the activity which neither takes time nor resources is called
explain: A dummy activity (also called redundant/null arrow) is used solely to show logical precedence without consuming time or resources.

q: 91. The maximum number of tail event occurring in a CPM is
explain: A proper network diagram has only one single initial start event (tail event for the overall project).

q: 92. The maximum number of head event occurring in a CPM is
explain: A properly constructed CPM network concludes at a single final completion event (head event).

q: 93. The maximum number of redundant activity in a CPM chart may be
explain: Depending on complex dependency connections, a network can contain zero or multiple dummy (redundant) activities.

q: 94. The activity which consumes maximum time is called
explain: A critical activity is defined as an activity having zero total float, not simply the one that takes the longest individual duration.

q: 95. The number of post-activity associated with head event may be
explain: The final terminal head event of a project marks overall completion, so it has zero succeeding (post) activities.

q: 96. The post-operations in CPM are marked
explain: Standard CPM networks read chronologically from left to right, placing succeeding (post) operations to the right.

q: 97. In CPM method, the earliest finish is indicated by time on
options: top right, outside the circle, in triangle
top right, outside the circle, in rectangle
explain: By common graphical notation, Earliest Finish times are marked inside a rectangle on the top right above the event/activity arrow.

q: 98. Latest finish time in CPM technique is indicated by
explain: Rectangles or square symbols are standard visual markers for time bounds (Earliest/Latest times) in CPM diagrams.

q: 99. When the times of earliest finish and the latest finish are equal in an operation, the operation is called
explain: When Earliest Finish equals Latest Finish, Total Float is zero, which defines a critical activity.

q: 100. An example for a parallel activity is
options: completing ground floor and starting first floor
wall and carpentry work of doors and windows
completion of flooring and initiating white washing
digging of a well and of septic tank
explain: Parallel activities occur concurrently. Masonry wall construction and off-site carpentry frame fabrication can take place at the same time.
